notes.note: One electron on a ring that holds 2, so 1 hand and exactly one bond. It's the plug that fills carbon's leftover hands.
Pyrolysis is hydrogen-limited: polyethylene has only 2 H per carbon, so not every broken chain can cap itself into methane. The shortfall pushes some carbon toward char.
Triethylborane is the TEB in TEA-TEB, the mix that ignites on contact with liquid oxygen and lights Merlin engines with a green flash.
4 hands, always 4 bonds. Methane gives all 4 hands to hydrogens; in a polyethylene chain, 2 hands hold the neighboring carbons and 2 hold hydrogens.
C-C bonds are weaker than C-H, so heat snaps chains first. Broken ends become methane, oil, wax or char depending on hydrogen and time at temperature.
Carbon is an atom, not a molecule. Each extra CH2 in a chain adds one carbon and two hydrogens.
CH2 on its own still has 2 empty hands, so it can't last. Two of them joined make ethylene; thousands in a row make polyethylene.
2 hands, 2 bonds. Double-bonds twice to carbon in CO2; holds one hydrogen in each hand in water. Sabatier swaps carbon's two oxygens for four hydrogens.
Liquid oxygen is most of a methalox rocket's propellant mass.
Aluminum swaps into zeolite frameworks and creates the acid sites that crack chains.
Falcon 9 uses aluminum-lithium tanks; Starship went to stainless steel instead. Triethylaluminum is the TEA in Falcon 9's TEA-TEB igniter.
Zeolite and clay catalyst powders, one lever for cutting char, are silicon-aluminum-oxygen frameworks with acid sites inside their pores.
Starship's ~18,000 heat-shield tiles are reported to be silica-based ceramic. The weak point is the joint between brittle tile and steel, which expand very differently.
The 'stainless' in Starship's stainless steel: chromium forms a thin oxide skin that heals itself and stops rust.
Starship is stainless steel, mostly iron. Steel stays strong both at cryogenic propellant temperatures and when hot on reentry, and it's cheap.
The catalyst in the Sabatier reaction: CO2 + 4H2 → CH4 + 2H2O. SpaceX's planned route to making methane on Mars. Nickel is also in stainless steel.
Your example: one loose 4s electron per atom joins a shared electron sea, which is why copper conducts. Copper alloys also line regeneratively cooled rocket chambers.
